title: Hand Block Print vs Screen Print: How to Tell the Difference
excerpt: How to tell real hand block printing from screen or digital prints – five simple checks, and why the small 'imperfections' matter.
body:
Many clothes are sold as 'block print' today, but not all of them are printed by hand. Here is how to tell the difference.

## What is hand block printing?

In hand block printing, a karigar (artisan) presses a hand-carved wooden block, dipped in colour, onto fabric – again and again, along a long padded table. Each colour in the design usually needs its own block. It is a slow craft that has been practised in and around Jaipur, in places like Sanganer and Bagru, for generations.

## 1. Look for tiny variations

In a real block print, the same motif will look very slightly different each time – a little lighter here, a slightly thicker line there. Screen and digital prints look perfectly identical.

## 2. Check where the motifs meet

Where one stamp meets the next, you may see a faint overlap or a tiny gap. This is the mark of a hand-placed block.

## 3. Look at the back of the fabric

Block printing colour usually soaks through the fabric, so the back shows the design clearly. Many digital prints look pale or blank on the back.

## 4. Feel the fabric

Hand block prints are usually done on natural fabrics like cotton, and the fabric stays soft and breathable.

## 5. Ask about the process

A genuine maker will happily tell you where and how the fabric was printed. At Bahe Kurtiz, our fabrics are block printed by karigars in Jaipur and stitched in our own unit.

## Why the 'imperfections' are a good thing

The small variations are not flaws – they show that a person made your outfit by hand. No two pieces are exactly alike.
